newsitem.title: UK: HSBC dragged down by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: HSBC dragged down by profit-taking.

text.p: Shares in Anglo-Hong Kong banking group HSBC Holdings Plc dropped on Monday as some investors opted to cash in gains after their record-breaking run last week, dealers said.
The stock was down 36-1/2p at 18.21 by 0832 GMT in volume of 830,275 shares, after on Friday touching a record 18.68 stg -- up some 15 percent on its level at the end of April.
"The whole sector is overbought," said market-maker in the stock. "There is definitely going to be some switching into other sectors."

Among other banks, Barclays Plc was down 3p at 12.52 stg, Lloyds TSB Plc was down 5p at 615-1/2 and Royal Bank of Scotland Plc -- which on Friday leapt 33p on speculation of a bid from HSBC -- was down 7-1/2p at 628.

The decline in bank stocks came despite upbeat press comment on the sector. The influential Lex column on Saturday said the sector contined to have appeal, since banks were generating large amounts of cash and dividends should "comfortably outpace the market for the next few years."
